translation_notes: URIRef('http://another') -> <http://another> and namespaces.HYCL.claims -> hycl:claims (with @prefix hycl: <http://purl.org/petapico/o/hycl#> .); the tuple and the .add() call keep their exact shape.

NEGATIVE FINDING: the flagship 'G += g{ ... }' form is unusable here. np.assertion is a read-only @property of Nanopub, and 'np.assertion += g{...}' compiles to a STORE_ATTR, so it raises AttributeError: property 'assertion' of 'Nanopub' object has no setter. Adding to a library graph reached through a property therefore needs either a local alias or, as here, the plain .add() call with island terms.

SECOND LIMITATION: Literal('hello') survives untouched. Outside an island a bare "hello" is a Python str, and rdflib's Graph.add() rejects it; only the suffixed literal forms ("x"@en, "x"^^t) are islands outside g{ }. So a plain, untyped, untagged literal is exactly the case the notation cannot shorten in argument position.

'from nanopub import namespaces' becomes dead on the ldpy side (the ontology IRI is inlined in the @prefix), the same trade-off already recorded for the siblings of this file: @prefix produces no runtime object and so does not track the library's own constant. The import line is kept as upstream.

demo harness added identically to both representations: the region is a pytest test that keeps its nanopub in a local and returns nothing, so the harness shadows Nanopub with a recording wrapper, runs the test, and republishes the assertion graph as module-level 'demo_assertion' for the isomorphism comparison. The test's own 'assert len(np.assertion) == 1' runs on both sides.
the driver puts the corpus checkout of commit 05022dc4bc on sys.path (sys.dont_write_bytecode) so the region's nanopub imports stay as upstream; no network is needed for this region.
